title: A lane dropped from two batches leaves the queue for a fix lane
why: Plan R26 part 2 (owner; restart-plan). Owner 13:15 CST Nov 12: "how do you propose us getting the merge queue faster?"
note: A lane dropped from two batches in a row leaves the merge queue and goes to a fix lane, so it stops holding later batches. Red first. Plan R55 (owner 13:19 and 13:21 CST Nov 12, restart-plan 4fefc9f, pick d: "Express lane, and cancel a running batch for it too"): a reviewed merge-flow lane goes to main as its own batch, ahead of all others; the batch runner cancels a batch run already in CI, and that batch then merges main in. Home: decision no-merge-during-batch-ci; skill ci-hygiene step 8 points to it (retrospective 13:23 CST, plan b152ca6). The owner chose this over the one-batch-in-turn rule. Takes a part of merge-batch-split-and-pipeline (coordinator split 13:36 CST Nov 12); R55 express, top of now (retrospective 13:38: owner 13:36 asked for the next batch to stack mechanically). Revised 13:43 CST Nov 12: takes the split-and-rebuild half of merge-batch-split-and-pipeline. Round-1 findings on the split work (archive/merge-batch-split-and-pipeline-2, head ee4da8508), coordinator 14:07 CST Nov 12: (a) a partial log read still drops and exits 0; (b) Blamed is written before batch_drop can refuse; (c) naming every lane drops all but one, then exits 1; (d) the --blame refusal wording changed; (e) no argparse cases for --batch-split. Owner item 634: does a split over-drop on a shared file (test_merge.py)? Item 634 closed 14:10 CST Nov 12, settled by decision batch-freeze-lane-set (a red run drops the one lane blame names, and its dependents): the split maps each red to the blamed lane, never drops by shared file.
